content_units: This 5-day routine is built for   25 minutes/day  , uses   one chair + one resistance band  , and aims to improve   mobility, leg strength, and confidence   without flaring knee pain.
- On   lisinopril  : rise slowly from chair/floor work and pause if lightheaded
- Best target effort:   easy to moderate   — about   3-5/10
- Mild muscle work is fine;   joint pain should stay low and settle within 24 hours
1   Mobility + basic leg strength   Sit-to-stand; band knee extension; calf raises; marching   25 min
2   Mobility + balance   Heel-toe raises; side leg raises; weight shifts; gentle stretching   25 min
3   Strength + posture   Sit-to-stand; seated band row; standing hamstring curl; calf raises   25 min
4   Recovery movement   Joint mobility circuit; short walking intervals indoors; stretching   25 min
5   Strength + control   Mini squat to chair; side steps with band; knee extension; balance hold   25 min
- March in place holding chair: 1 min
- Seated knee straighten/bend: 10 reps each leg
- Hip circles standing with chair support: 10 each way
- Seated band knee extension:   2 sets of 8-10 each leg
- Standing calf raises holding chair:   2 sets of 10
- Standing march with tall posture:   2 sets of 20-30 sec
- Seated hamstring stretch: 20 sec each side
- Calf stretch at wall/chair: 20 sec each side
- Easy indoor walking or marching: 2 min
- Knee bends holding chair, very shallow: 10 reps
- Heel digs forward alternating legs: 10 each
- Toe raises holding chair:   2 sets of 10
- Standing side leg raises:   2 sets of 8 each leg
- Side-to-side weight shifts:   2 sets of 30 sec
- Tandem or semi-tandem stand near chair:   3 rounds of 15-20 sec
- Seated figure-4 or gentle hip stretch: 20 sec each side
- Quad stretch modified in standing if comfortable: 15-20 sec each
- Seated knee extension without band: 10 each
- Standing hamstring curl holding chair:   2 sets of 8-10 each leg
- Easy walk around room for 1 min
- Ankle pumps and knee bends: 1 min
- Mini squat to chair touch:   2 sets of 6-8
- Side steps with band above knees or at ankles if easy:   2 sets of 6-8 steps each way
- Seated band knee extension:   2 sets of 10 each leg
- Single-leg balance with fingertips on chair:   3 rounds of 10-15 sec each
Stop the session and rest if any of these happen:
-   Sharp, stabbing, or catching knee pain
- Pain that rises above   4/10   during exercise
- Knee swelling, warmth, or limping that increases after the session
- Pain that does   not return to usual baseline by the next day
- Dizziness, faintness, unusual shortness of breath, chest pressure, or severe headache
-   Green:   discomfort   0-2/10  , feels worked but okay → continue
-   Yellow:   discomfort   3-4/10  , form worsening or soreness building → reduce range, slow down, or do fewer reps
-   Red:   discomfort   5+/10   or sharp pain → stop that exercise
Use these only if the knee feels okay during exercise and the next day.
- Start with   2 sets   for most moves
- First increase   reps  , then   band tension  , then   time
- Add only   one   change per week
- Week 4: add a   3rd set   to 1-2 exercises
- Week 5+: use a slightly tighter band or slower lowering phase
- For balance drills, add   5 seconds   at a time
- For marching/walking intervals, add   30 seconds   total
Form cues that protect the knee
- Keep knee tracking roughly over the   middle toes
- Use   small pain-free ranges   at first
- Sit back to the chair rather than pushing knees far forward
- Move slowly on the way down
- Hold the chair whenever balance feels uncertain
